season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is fully cleared from the Week 15 torn ACL/LCL and targeting the Week 1 Monday night opener vs Denver, so his 6-pt-per-TD premium is intact but early-season rust risk is real in a revamped run-heavier Chiefs offense.

Puka Nacua entered a Malibu rehab facility and league discipline could sideline him multiple games, pushing target and red-zone equity toward Davante Adams and checkdown/TD volume toward Kyren Williams in the NFL's highest win-total offense (11.5).

Josh Jacobs faces an open Brown County domestic violence investigation with a baseline six-game suspension on the table, so his TD-heavy goal-line role in Green Bay could vanish for half a season and his backfield handcuffs spike in value.

Four unresolved QB battles reshape draft boards: Tua Tagovailoa vs Michael Penix Jr. in Atlanta, Deshaun Watson vs Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland, Kyler Murray (vet-minimum) vs J.J. McCarthy in Minnesota, and Kirk Cousins holding off No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas.

Malik Nabers needed a second offseason surgery to clear scar tissue from his 2025 ACL tear and Week 1 is in doubt, which in a zero-PPR league further dents a catch-volume profile and funnels early-season Giants work to Wan'Dale Robinson and Cam Skattebo (verify).

Mike McDaniel takes over the Chargers offense as OC with a fully rebuilt interior line (Slaughter, Biadasz, Strange) after a franchise-record 54 sacks, a wide-zone YAC scheme that boosts Omarion Hampton's rushing yardage and Justin Herbert's efficiency.

Super Bowl champion Seattle lost MVP Kenneth Walker III and hands the backfield to first-round rookie Jadarian Price with Zach Charbonnet opening camp on PUP after an ACL tear, one of the cleanest paths to instant goal-line and yardage volume in the league.

Mike Evans left Tampa for San Francisco at age 33, clearing an alpha TD-scoring role for Emeka Egbuka under new McVay-tree OC Zac Robinson while Bucky Irving rehabs shoulder surgery, and Kenny Gainwell arrives off a 17.8-ppg late-2025 stretch (verify).

Betting markets set the Rams and Ravens at a league-high 11.5 wins and the Cardinals at a floor 3.5, so LAR/BAL skill players carry the best game-environment floors while Arizona assets outside No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love need volume, not wins.

Return jobs are worth roughly 2.5-3.4 ppg in this league's 20-yds/pt format: KaVontae Turpin (DAL), Marvin Mims Jr. (DEN), Parker Washington (JAX), Malik Washington (MIA), Keaton Mitchell (BAL) and rookie Chimere Dike (TEN) all have locked or expanding dual-return roles (verify roles in camp).

teams.outlook: First-year HC Mike LaFleur inherits a 3.5-win-total roster, and OC Nathaniel Hackett is slow-playing No. 3 pick Jeremiyah Love behind aging James Conner, so Love's league-winning goal-line takeover is a when-not-if but maybe not Week 1.

Kevin Stefanski's system (verify) hosts a messy QB battle between released-by-Miami Tua Tagovailoa and rehabbing Michael Penix Jr., capping every Falcons pass catcher including newly extended Kyle Pitts until it settles.

New HC Jesse Minter and first-time OC Declan Doyle bring motion-heavy outside zone at an 11.5 win total, a Lamar Jackson bounce-back environment, but a wide-open center battle after Tyler Linderbaum left for Vegas adds interior risk to Derrick Henry's lanes.
New HC Joe Brady keeps the offense built around Josh Allen's rushing TD floor at a 10.5 win total while DC Jim Leonhard rebuilds a 24th-in-pressures defense with Bradley Chubb and rookie T.J. Parker.

Bryce Young carries breakout momentum into camp, but both starting tackles (Ekwonu, Moton) are out with rookie Monroe Freeling flipping to right tackle, so the 7.5-win offense's protection is shakier than the buzz.

Ben Johnson calling plays for Caleb Williams at a 9.5 win total is the league's premier scheme upgrade, with 150 vacated targets making Luther Burden III's 2.92 YPRR profile a yardage-league breakout.

Cincinnati spent the offseason rebuilding the defense (Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe) around a 10.5 win total, which slightly cools the shootout script that made Bengals passers and receivers volume monsters.

HC Todd Monken must pick between Deshaun Watson (back from a full-year Achilles absence) and Shedeur Sanders at a 5.5 win total, and David Njoku's departure raises Harold Fannin Jr.'s price beyond his practice-time reality.

New DC Christian Parker imports Eagles concepts to fix the league's worst defense at a 9.5 win total, while Brandon Aubrey's 60-yard leg and KaVontae Turpin's dual-return role are elite fits for this league's distance-kicker and return-yardage scoring.

Bo Nix returns from the broken ankle suffered in the divisional-round OT win, and a new No. 1 target (Jaylen Waddle, verify) plus Marvin Mims Jr.'s All-Pro return role support a 9.5-win offense with sneaky yardage upside.

New OC Drew Petzing wants to unlock Jameson Williams downfield, a deep-threat profile this league's yardage scoring loves, while a 10.5-win offense stays elite and the defense sweats Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph both opening on PUP.

OC Adam Stenavich called it 'a big year' for Matthew Golden after trimming the WR room, but Josh Jacobs' open suspension risk, Tucker Kraft's torn ACL and Micah Parsons' ACL loss cloud a 9.5-win roster on both sides.

Houston reset around C.J. Stroud with O-line upgrades and David Montgomery's goal-line hammer at a 9.5 win total, while rookie Jayden Higgins is positioned to eat with Christian Kirk gone and Tank Dell still rehabbing.
Daniel Jones says he is a full go for camp off a Week 16 torn Achilles after his $88M extension, and his rushing floor in Shane Steichen's spread keeps him a 6-pt-TD value if the recovery holds.

Travis Hunter is fully cleared from his torn LCL but will play primarily cornerback with WR rotation work, Brian Thomas Jr. is the drops-fixed bounce-back bet, and Bhayshul Tuten inherits the vacated lead-back role at 8.5 wins.

Mahomes is cleared for camp nine months post ACL/LCL with a revamped rushing attack built to protect him, and Rashee Rice is expected to avoid NFL suspension after serving his 30-day jail sentence, restoring KC's 10.5-win TD equity.

Mike McDaniel's wide-zone, motion-heavy scheme plus three new interior linemen turn a 54-sack disaster into a 9.5-win offense where Omarion Hampton's power running and Ladd McConkey's separation profile both rise.

A league-high 11.5 win total meets chaos: Puka Nacua is in rehab with multi-game discipline possible, 38-year-old Matthew Stafford is a fade-the-age passer, and Myles Garrett's arrival has Aaron Donald openly flirting with unretirement.

HC Klint Kubiak starts Kirk Cousins while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza pushes for early snaps amid a contract dispute, and Ashton Jeanty is the main 5.5-win-team asset behind newly acquired center Tyler Linderbaum.

A teardown with 23 rookies and nearly $180M in dead cap leaves Malik Willis at QB and a wide-open target tree at 4.5 wins, where Malik Washington's full-time dual-return job is the roster's most bankable fantasy points.

Kyler Murray on a veteran minimum is battling J.J. McCarthy (last in completion rate and TD-INT as a rookie) in Kevin O'Connell's QB-friendly system, and whoever wins inherits an 8.5-win offense with concentrated WR value.

Drake Maye gets A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and an upgraded line at a 10.5 win total, a genuine TD-equity leap, though the front office is distracted by making Christian Gonzalez the highest-paid CB in football.
Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus-point games and now adds No. 8 pick Jordyn Tyson next to Chris Olave, making the 7.5-win Saints a sneaky pace-up passing environment.

New OC Matt Nagy's West Coast spread leans on Jaxson Dart's mobility at 7.5 wins, with Malik Nabers' second knee procedure leaving Wan'Dale Robinson and Cam Skattebo (verify) as the early-season volume beneficiaries.
Geno Smith lands behind a much better line than the one that allowed a league-high 55 sacks in Vegas, but a 5.5 win total and thin skill corps cap everything except best-ball dart throws.

First-time OC Sean Mannion installs a Shanahan-LaFleur wide-zone attack after Jalen Hurts' career-low 7.1 YPA season, expanding Saquon Barkley's receiving role and leaving DeVonta Smith an uncontested target share at 10.5 wins.

Mike McCarthy's first Steelers camp pairs him with Aaron Rodgers in his announced final season at 8.5 wins, a short-area system whose low-INT profile fits this league's -2 INT scoring better than its ceiling suggests.

The defending champs lost Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III and OC continuity (Brian Fleury takes over), handing first-rounder Jadarian Price a clear shot at lead early-down and goal-line work with Charbonnet on PUP at 10.5 wins.

Kyle Shanahan is coaching through injuries from a car crash but expects Week 1, where 33-year-old Mike Evans, a 450-touch Christian McCaffrey and Achilles-rehabbing George Kittle make the 9.5-win 49ers talented, old and fragile.
McVay-tree OC Zac Robinson inherits a post-Evans offense at 8.5 wins where Emeka Egbuka is the new alpha, Bucky Irving rehabs shoulder surgery, and Baker Mayfield plays for a $50M-plus extension.

Brian Daboll's RPO and play-action-vertical install is built to force Cam Ward's Year 2 leap (11 TD, 2 INT over his final seven starts) at 6.5 wins, with rookie Chimere Dike locked into dual return duties for cheap extra points.

Dan Quinn hands the offense to first-time coordinator David Blough and rebuilt the front seven (Chenal, Oweh, Chaisson) at a modest 7.5 win total, a mild downgrade to the offensive environment until Blough proves it.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Fractured ankle hid his rookie talent for 7 games; now the engine of Mike McDaniel's wide-zone scheme behind a rebuilt Chargers interior line, a pure rushing-yardage and TD profile that non-PPR loves.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: First-round pick walks into the champs' vacated Kenneth Walker III role with Charbonnet on PUP; early-down and goal-line work on a 10.5-win team is exactly this league's gold.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall picks at RB have a near-automatic top-12 rookie hit rate; Hackett is slow-playing him behind James Conner, so he is a discounted mid-season goal-line monopoly.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Inherits Jacksonville's lead-back vacancy after converting 7 of 93 touches into TDs with a 31% missed-tackle rate, an elite TD-per-touch profile stepping into volume.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Dramatically improved Raiders line (Linderbaum), scheme and coaching around him; volume is guaranteed on a run-first Kubiak offense even at a 5.5 win total.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Ben Johnson play-calling, Caleb Williams throwing, and 150 vacated Bears targets meet a 2.92 yards-per-route-run profile; his YAC yardage scores full price in 10-yds/pt scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure hands him the Bucs' alpha X role and its red-zone targets under McVay-tree OC Zac Robinson after four 20-point rookie games.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Matched Nico Collins' 6 TDs on far less volume as a rookie; Christian Kirk gone and Tank Dell still rehabbing leave him a full-time perimeter TD role in a reset Texans offense.

breakout_watch.name: Jameson Williams
breakout_watch.why: New Lions OC Drew Petzing is explicitly building around his vertical speed; deep-ball yardage and long TDs beat slot volume in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight 17-plus-point games to close 2025, now adding No. 8 pick Jordyn Tyson and more weapons; a cheap 6-pt-TD QB with rushing juice on an overachieving offense.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: 11 TD to 2 INT over his final seven starts, and Brian Daboll's QB-development track record targets exactly the INT cleanup this league's -2 penalty demands.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: Matt Nagy's West Coast spread is built around his legs; rushing yardage plus 6-pt passing TDs gives him a weekly ceiling his 7.5-win team total hides.

breakout_watch.name: Keaton Mitchell
breakout_watch.why: Praised all offseason as Baltimore's primary returner while backing up an aging Henry; return yardage at 20 yds/pt plus home-run rushing speed makes him a roster-clogger with spike weeks.

breakout_watch.name: Chimere Dike
breakout_watch.why: Locked in as Tennessee's kick and punt returner as a rookie; a near-guaranteed 2.5-3 ppg return-yardage floor before he runs a single route (verify camp confirmation).

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Open domestic violence investigation with a baseline six-game suspension possible, age 28 with 2,109 career touches and YPC already down to 4.0; the TD role is elite but could evaporate in one league announcement.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age-and-workload cliff behind a Ravens line breaking in a brand-new center; his value is entirely TD-and-yardage, and both erode fast when interior push slips.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off a 450-touch season at an age where historical data shows sharp regression; much of his value is receptions, which are worth zero here.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Second knee surgery to remove scar tissue and a shaky Week 1 outlook; his catch-volume profile is discounted in zero-PPR even at full health.

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age-33 season on a new team after a career-low 12.1 PPG, moving into a Shanahan offense that spreads TD equity around.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age 38 with his top receiver in rehab facing possible suspension; even at a league-high 11.5 win total the arrow on his passing yardage and TD counts points down.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: Defenses adjusted late in 2025 and a new OC changes the target tree; TE catch volume without TDs is near-worthless in this scoring.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: Njoku's exit is inflating his price while he logged suspiciously little offseason practice time on a 5.5-win offense with an unsettled QB.

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: Classic post-breakout regression profile, and Jonathon Brooks is cleared and pushing for the valuable goal-line share behind a patchwork Panthers line.

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled as of Aug 1: all four QB battles (ATL, CLE, MIN, LV) are unresolved; the NFL has announced nothing on Puka Nacua discipline or Josh Jacobs' investigation; Week 1 availability is unconfirmed for Malik Nabers, George Kittle and (rust-wise) Mahomes; Travis Etienne's landing spot is reported inconsistently across sources (Saints FA visit vs Texans signing - verify); Jaylen Waddle's team (DEN vs TEN) also conflicts across reports; and Aaron Donald's unretirement is pure speculation.
